Commented-out README note references XLand-100B dataset (github.com/dunno-lab/xland-minigrid-datasets) 'based on XLand-MiniGrid'. || main loop (reader, from the code): Environment.step applies the agent's action to the grid (take_action), then lax.scan's over the task's encoded production rules (check_rule, lax.switch dispatch per rule) to transform grid/agent, then evaluates the encoded goal (check_goal) to decide termination and a time-discounted reward of 1 - 0.9*step/max_steps, truncating at max_steps; the meta-training loop (train_meta_task.make_train) samples a fresh batch of rulesets from a Benchmark each meta-update and runs recurrent PPO over multi-trial rollouts.

organs.mechanism: a goal is drawn uniformly over 11 types; each open tile is either pruned (p = prune_prob, default 0.5 when --prune_chain) into an initial tile or given a rule that produces it from tiles not yet used, whose inputs become the next layer; distractor objects and dead-end rules are added; exact-encoding duplicates are rejected
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: deep chains without pruning can exhaust the 60-tile pool (random.choice on an empty list); deduplication is on the exact encoding, so reordered rules count as new

organs.mechanism: sample_ruleset is randint over a fixed benchmark; each environment redraws per meta-step; the code comment invites custom curricula but none exists
organs.failure_landscape: by reading (MEDIUM): the meta-training script evaluates on the same benchmark object it trains on; a split() exists but is not called there

organs.mechanism: reward = 1.0 - 0.9 * step_num / max_steps when the goal is met, else 0; termination zeroes the discount; truncation at max_steps (default 3 * height * width)

every step each rule encoding is scanned through a 12-way switch (e.g. holding tile T while acting turns it into P; standing near T turns it into P) and the goal through a 15-way switch; the code itself notes that rules fire only on certain actions
